A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MOOSE-Star work. The complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated appendix content.

before.justification: v2 reports original retrieval, hypothesis-composition, training-scaling, and inference-scaling experiments, plus appendix ablations and temporal reconstruction results.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical evaluations and adds sampling diagnostics and controlled context ablations in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Decomposed retrieval/composition training, bounded composition, hierarchical best-first search, and motivation planning remain unchanged. Corrected delta indexing and expanded descriptions do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: The TOMATO-Star corpus, scientific domains, temporal coverage, and discovery tasks remain unchanged. Appendix D adds a limited input scenario in which the research question is retained but the background survey is withheld.

E2.justification: The frontier-model, base-model, random-selection, tournament-search, and brute-force comparator sets are retained. Table 5 newly reports the proposed IR subtask's sampling yield; this is additional component evaluation rather than a new baseline.

E3.justification: Table 5 substantially revises reported sample counts: BF changes from 110,314 to 59,933 and HC from 195,301 to 1,552,624 attempts. Appendix D adds controlled evaluations on 500 three-inspiration papers using regenerated R1-Distilled-Qwen-32B outputs and Gemini-3-Flash judging. The PDFs do not establish how all earlier and later attempts correspond.

E4.justification: New Tables 7–8 analyze scores by inspiration depth and composition-step position. Table 9 ablates the background survey and previous hypothesis state to investigate the source of HC's later-step advantage. Earlier retrieval-shortcut ablations and the temporal case study are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 3 retains four pairwise judgments: two independent trials, each with original and swapped positions. No confidence intervals, significance tests, or seed-based variability reporting are added. The new ablation's four generated outputs per paper specify its sampling budget.

E6.justification: Table 5 replaces overall BF and HC pass rates of 0.67% and 49.60% with 3.48% and 22.62%, and adds IR's 25.59%. These use different reported denominators and are not same-setting performance improvements. New Tables 7–9 add diagnostic results; Tables 1–4, Figure 2–3 results, and relocated temporal results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendix E introduces instance-specific failure probabilities and derives pass@T = 1 - mean(p_i^T) under independent attempts, using this model to explain sampling saturation. The original complexity arguments and Appendix B decomposition assumptions and derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The central claims about intractability, tractable and scalable decomposed training, best-case logarithmic search, test-time scaling, and the dataset release remain. v4 emphasizes training-data scaling in the abstract and conclusion, but v2 already makes and supports that claim in Section 7.2.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive explanations of HC's context-dependent pass-rate drift and BF saturation, and distinguishes Table 5's per-attempt rates from Figure 3's paper-level measures. It replaces 'statistically impossible' sampling language with practical-budget qualifications and adds explicit proposal-versus-feedback boundaries and experimental-validation limitations.

D1.justification: v4 explicitly identifies MS-IR-7B as the routing model and MS-7B versus R1-Distilled-Qwen-7B in Figure 3. It also clarifies concatenation of step outputs and reference-derived training histories. These are documentation additions; code/data access information and reported GPU costs remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds Levi's inference-scaling work and MOOSE-Chem3, removes the Intern-S1 and AlphaFold citations, and revises its characterization of O'Neill et al.'s paper-derived supervision. Its principal positioning around training the hypothesis proposal distribution is retained.

P1.justification: The scaling discussion is condensed and reorganized, including explicit Cost, Success, and Results paragraphs. Introductory wording and publication information are edited. New appendices are inserted while the earlier temporal evaluation and rubric move from D/E to F/H; most existing exposition remains.

P2.justification: Table 5 is reorganized into BF, HC, and IR columns with rates and counts, and three diagnostic tables are added. Existing displays are relocated, while Figure 3's legend and caption clarify per-inspiration sampling and model identities. The overall visual format remains stable.

improvement.justification: v4 strengthens the empirical argument through controlled context ablations with an independent judge and clearer sampling accounting. It also makes Figure 3 easier to interpret by distinguishing BF win-or-tie coverage from MOOSE-Star pipeline completion. These improve transparency and diagnostic support, while the central method and main benchmark findings remain stable and prospective experimental validation remains outside the study.
